cases.setup: Provide a pinned public checkout exhibiting a false unused-import warning for an imported type in a quoted TypeAlias value and no warning for the same reference in a quoted function annotation. Make handler code and marker bindings publicly accessible.
checks: The inspection report contains the pinned revision and hashed current code anchors for annotated-assignment handling, typing-marker resolution, and annotation-value handling.
Recorded analyzer output contains the unused-import warning for the alias fixture and no unused-import warning for the comparison fixture.
The report identifies the alias value's current ordinary-expression dispatch and the comparison's annotation-processing dispatch using current code anchors.
The report records alias-dispatch-applicable as PASS only after reviewing marker identity and both dispatch paths; unresolved facts are UNKNOWN.
The emitted inspected-checkout PortValue has language python, scope current-public-checkout, phase repair, and state inspected.
A before/after checkout diff shows no source or test modifications from inspection.

cases.setup: Provide an inspected checkout with applicability PASS and all handler roles bound. Include fixtures for recognized quoted and unquoted TypeAlias values, an ordinary annotated string value, and a no-value TypeAlias declaration.
checks: The implementation diff shows a present-value conditional using the existing scope-aware typing-marker resolver.
The recognized TypeAlias branch invokes the existing annotation-value handler; the non-marker branch retains the existing ordinary-expression handler.
Current code review or public handler tracing shows target and marker annotation processing still occurs for annotated assignments.
The no-value fixture does not invoke any value handler.
The ordinary annotated string fixture remains on the ordinary-expression path rather than entering annotation-string processing.
The output PortValue has state value-routing-patched, and observations for current alias diagnostics, adjacent diagnostics, and regression results are marked stale.
The current plan retains explicit-type-alias-string-analysis.validate with validation_for containing explicit-type-alias-string-analysis.route.

cases.setup: Provide a value-routing-patched checkout with its implementation diff reviewed and a bound public annotation regression test owner. Preserve a snapshot of existing assertions for comparison.
checks: Inspection of the test diff finds assertions for imported type values in all four combinations of module/class scope and quoted/unquoted value.
Each of the four value cases explicitly expects an empty diagnostic set.
A no-value TypeAlias case explicitly expects an empty diagnostic set.
A no-value TypeAlias case with an otherwise unused imported type explicitly expects that type's unused-import diagnostic.
Comparison with the supplied test snapshot shows existing assertions have not been removed or weakened.
The emitted checkout PortValue has state regressions-present; regression execution observations are invalidated rather than marked PASS merely because assertions exist.
The current plan retains explicit-type-alias-string-analysis.validate with validation_for containing explicit-type-alias-string-analysis.tests.

cases.setup: Provide the final regression checkout and current public Oracle bindings for the reproduction and annotation suite. Each binding includes an instruction, argv command, and public evidence references. Ensure the six regression fixtures and ordinary-value boundary are available for execution or public inspection.
checks: The report renders the actual current argv commands under oracle:explicit-type-alias-string-analysis.validate:quoted-alias-reproduction and oracle:explicit-type-alias-string-analysis.validate:alias-and-adjacent-regressions before recording execution results.
Captured reproduction diagnostics contain no false unused-import warning for the quoted alias, and the quoted function-annotation comparison remains free of that warning.
Captured regression results show no diagnostics for the four module/class quoted/unquoted value cases and the isolated no-value case.
The no-value control produces the expected unused-import diagnostic for the unrelated imported type.
The report includes the annotation suite's command exit status and test summary, plus current evidence that ordinary non-TypeAlias values retain expression processing.
The report assigns PASS, FAIL, or UNKNOWN separately to each required behavioral check and names the exact files or suites exercised.
Previously invalidated diagnostic and test observations are replaced with results from the final checkout rather than reused from the base.
The report does not accept the repair if any adjacent-behavior check is FAIL or any required validation is UNKNOWN.
A before/after source and test diff shows validation made no additional repair edits.
The report explicitly states that changed-test-only qualification proves neither whole-project regression safety nor cross-project transfer.
